questions.stem: A 'biosphere reserve' in India is a zone that:

options.option_text: Protects biodiversity while allowing sustainable human use within a buffer zone

questions.explanation: Biosphere Reserves (UNESCO concept): Core zone (no human activity), Buffer zone (limited research/tourism), Transition zone (sustainable use by local communities). India has 18 biosphere reserves.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The 'Paris Agreement' on climate change aims to limit global temperature rise to:

options.option_text: Well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, striving for 1.5°C

questions.explanation: Paris Agreement (2015, entered into force 2016): limit warming to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C. India's NDC: 45% emissions intensity reduction by 2030.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Chipko Movement (1973) was a grassroots forest conservation movement in:
questions.explanation: Chipko (hug the trees): women of Reni village, Chamoli district led by Gaura Devi hugged trees to prevent logging (1973). Inspired by Amrita Devi Bishnoi's earlier 18th-century tree protection.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Which treaty addresses the international trade in endangered species?

options.option_text: CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species)

questions.explanation: CITES (1973): regulates international wildlife trade. Appendix I (most threatened, trade banned), Appendix II (controlled), Appendix III (country-specific protection). India is a signatory.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The 'ozone hole' was primarily caused by which chemical compounds?

options.option_text: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) used in refrigerants and aerosols

questions.explanation: CFCs (Freon gas): when they reach the stratosphere, UV light breaks them down, releasing chlorine atoms that destroy ozone (O3). Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out CFCs.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The 'Green India Mission' is one of eight missions under:

options.option_text: National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)

questions.explanation: NAPCC (2008): 8 National Missions including Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Eco-system, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, and Strategic Knowledge.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Western Ghats is one of the world's biodiversity hotspots. How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are in the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats (declared UNESCO World Heritage Site 2012) includes 39 serial sites across Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra. Home to 325 globally threatened species.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Project Tiger was launched in India in:
questions.explanation: Project Tiger launched on 1 April 1973 with 9 tiger reserves. Currently India has 54 tiger reserves. India has ~75% of world's wild tigers (2022 count: 3,167).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Sundarbans, a mangrove forest and UNESCO World Heritage Site, spans:
questions.explanation: Sundarbans spans the Bengal delta across India (West Bengal, ~4200 sq km) and Bangladesh (~6000 sq km). Largest mangrove forest; home to Bengal tigers and Irrawaddy dolphins.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Eutrophication of water bodies is caused by:

options.option_text: Excess nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus) causing algal bloom, depleting dissolved oxygen

questions.explanation: Eutrophication: nutrient enrichment (from fertiliser runoff) → algal bloom → algae die → decomposition consumes O2 → dead zone (hypoxia). Fish and aquatic life suffocate.
questions.subject: Environment

options.option_text: Conservation and sustainable use of wetlands

questions.explanation: Ramsar Convention (1971, Iran): first modern intergovernmental treaty on conservation. India has 75+ Ramsar sites (as of 2022). Chilika Lake was India's first (1981).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The 'albedo effect' in climate science refers to:

options.option_text: The reflectivity of surfaces — higher albedo reflects more solar radiation back to space
The absorption of CO2 by forests
The warming effect of dark ocean surfaces
The formation of clouds over ocean surfaces

questions.explanation: Albedo = fraction of sunlight reflected. Ice/snow: high albedo (~0.9). Dark ocean: low albedo (~0.06). Melting ice reduces albedo → more heat absorbed → more melting (positive feedback loop).
